About Meridial

Meridial places skilled, remote-first professionals into high-trust, high-precision operational opportunities for leading technology companies. Our teams work as an embedded extension of our clients' own product and operations organizations, holding the same quality bar and the same deadlines.

The Opportunity

As an SMB AI Power User on the Competitive Evaluations team, you'll help a major consumer technology company find out where its bundled AI assistant subscription falls short of the standalone assistants small businesses already pay for. You are not an AI researcher studying the problem from the outside - you are a working or experienced business owner who already runs on these tools, and your own operations are the test bed.

Your day is spent doing what you already do: drafting ad copy, planning content, answering customer messages, researching suppliers, and reconciling numbers. The difference is that you do it across competing assistants, side by side, and document precisely where each one breaks. The failures you surface are the failures real paying subscribers will hit, which is exactly why the seat calls for a genuine operator rather than an evaluator.



What You'll Do

  • Run head-to-head prompts and multi-turn workflows across the client's assistant and competing paid assistants, using tasks drawn from your own business operations and marketing.
  • Build and maintain a library of realistic small-business test cases spanning ad creative and copy, organic content planning, customer messaging, competitor research, pricing, scheduling, and light bookkeeping.
  • Identify and document failure modes - wrong answers, unnecessary refusals, weak instruction-following, tone misses, brand-unsafe output, broken formatting, context lost across turns, unusable image or video output.
  • Write clear, reproducible reports: prompt used, model and surface, expected output, actual output, severity, and why the failure matters to a paying business subscriber.
  • Assess the bundled subscription on value terms - what a business owner actually receives versus what a standalone competitor subscription delivers for comparable spend.
  • Stress-test assistant features inside the social and commerce surfaces where business owners meet them, not only the standalone chat product.

 

What We're Looking For

  • Owner or operator of a small or medium business - sole proprietor, founder, or the person running day-to-day operations at a business of roughly 1–200 employees.
  • Daily, habitual use of generative AI tools in that business, for both operations and marketing. Experimental or occasional use is not a fit.
  • Organic presence on Instagram and Facebook for the business, maintained personally: posting, Stories, Reels, comment and message response.
  • Hands-on paid advertising experience on Meta platforms - has personally built, launched, and optimized campaigns with real budget.
  • Based in the United States and authorized to work here.
  • Capacity sufficient to complete deliverables per the agreed scope and timeline, which may include up to 40 hours per week 
  • Exceptional written English - able to describe a failure clearly enough that an engineer can reproduce it without follow-up.
  • Comfortable working independently against a rubric and holding a weekly output cadence.

Nice to Have

  • At least one current paid AI subscription (ChatGPT Plus/Pro, Claude Pro/Max, Gemini Advanced, or similar), so competitive comparison rests on actual use.
  • Runs a side business or second venture alongside a primary role - the profile that tends to test AI hardest against limited time.
  • Heavy Instagram user, personally and commercially: fluent in Reels, Stories, trends, and creator tooling.
  • Subscribes to two or more AI assistants simultaneously and holds an informed view on where each one wins.
  • Uses AI beyond chat - automations, agents, API or no-code integrations, custom GPTs or Projects.
  • Prior experience with model evaluation, red teaming, data annotation, QA, or structured user research.
  • Working familiarity with adjacent SMB tooling: Shopify, Square, QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Canva, CapCut, Later, or similar.
  • Industry range across the two hires - for example, one services or retail operator alongside one e-commerce or creator-economy operator.

Java Coding Specialist - Freelance AI Trainer Project United States of America

Are you a Java expert who can spot a flawed abstraction from across a codebase? Large-scale language models are evolving from clever chatbots into engines of real scientific and engineering progress. High-quality training data is what separates a capable model from a genuinely useful one. That data starts with people who actually know the craft.

We're looking for Java specialists with deep fluency in object-oriented design, concurrency, JVM internals, data structures, algorithms, and system architecture. You'll put advanced language models through their paces on Java problems spanning a wide range of difficulty and complexity, assessing whether model-generated solutions are correct, well-reasoned, and production-quality. That means evaluating not just whether code runs, but whether it's the right approach, whether edge cases are handled, and whether the reasoning behind it holds up.

You'll review Java problems and model-generated solutions, judge correctness and code quality, identify where the model's logic breaks down, and document failure patterns clearly enough that others can act on them. You may also flag whether a given problem is well-specified and appropriately challenging for training purposes.

A bachelor's, master's, or PhD in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field is a strong signal. So is real-world Java experience, competitive programming, open-source contributions, or technical writing. The ability to clearly articulate why a solution is wrong or weak, not just that it is, matters as much as the technical depth.

Ready to put your Java expertise to work shaping the next generation of AI? Apply today.

You'll build integrations with external systems, configure AI-powered document verification workflows, develop automations, and work closely with our product and engineering teams to solve customer-specific challenges.

This is a hands-on engineering role where you'll write code, solve real-world technical problems, interact directly with customers, and see the impact of your work in live enterprise environments.

ABOUT SWEETSPOT HEATING & COOLING

SweetSpot is a growing home-services company in the New York metro, and we are building our creative team from zero. This is the number one creative seat in the company, not a slot in a large agency hierarchy. The strategist hired here owns the function, works directly with the owner, and has a real path to leading the team as we scale.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring a creative strategist who will own paid ad creative end to end: research, angles, hooks, scripts, briefing creators and editors, and the learnings that turn winners into the next batch.

This is not a "make pretty ads" role and it is not strategy-only. You will direct really strong video editors and UGC creators, and you will use AI (including Claude Code) as your production engine for research, hooks, scripts and variants. We are honest about the level this role is hired at: we are looking for strong raw talent with real direct-response instincts who wants ownership and serious training, and who wants to grow into a top-tier strategist with us. You will get mentorship, a proven creative system, and weekly learnings reviews. In return we expect pace, curiosity, and work you can defend.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Build the research base first: homeowner avatars, desires, objections, competitors, and our own ad account history. No angles before research.

 - Plan concepts in a structured roadmap, each with angle, avatar, desire, mechanism, authority, awareness level, emotion, positioning and urgency.

 - Write hooks and scripts built for the first 3 seconds: one desire, one avatar, one message per ad.

 - Brief UGC creators and editors so clearly they can execute with no follow-up call, and review their work to a finished, launch-ready ad.

 - Run the testing system: from one winning angle, build structured iterations where each variation tests something named.

 - Run the learnings: label every ad (Breakthrough, Spend Winner, KPI Winner, Loser), state why it performed, and turn that into the next round.

 - Hit 20 to 30 finished, launch-ready ads per month at full pace, working with our editors and AI workflows.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Direct-response ad experience: you have written ads that ran as paid social (Meta or TikTok) and you can show them.

 - A testing system, not just good taste. You can explain how you turn one winner into 20 variations.

 - Research discipline. Your hooks trace to evidence, not guesses.

 - AI fluency: you already use AI tools in your creative workflow and can show how.

 - Execution: you have briefed creators or managed editors and shipped finished ads.

 - Ownership mindset: you talk about business outcomes, not just outputs delivered, and you close feedback loops: you learn, you apply, you show what changed.

 - Local services or lead generation experience is a plus, not a requirement. Seasonal urgency, emergency calls, proof and trust are the game here.


PAY AND STRUCTURE

 - Contract (1099), remote, month-to-month: $4,000 to $8,000 per month, 40 hours per week, based on experience.

 - Performance bonus structure discussed after the trial month, tied to winning ads.

 - Growth path: this seat grows into leading the creative team. One of the paths we model is editor or strategist to team lead as spend scales.


OUR HIRING PROCESS (EXACTLY HOW IT WORKS)

 1. Short application: portfolio of ads you wrote that actually ran, plus 3 short answers (your testing system on a real winner; one ad you iterated and what it tested; your AI workflow).

 2. Interview 1 (30 minutes): screening and craft in one call, run as a working session on your past ads: what did you learn, how did you apply it, what feedback loops did you complete.

 3. Paid test: $100 flat, 48 hours, capped at 4 hours of work, paid regardless of outcome. A short research snapshot, hooks, scripts, an iteration plan and an execution plan for a real scenario.

 4. Interview 2 (final, with the owner): we walk your test together and you defend your choices. References are checked after this call (we will ask to speak with one past employer). Two interviews total, no more.

 5. Paid 30-day trial at your full agreed monthly rate, with daily contact, mentorship and a weekly check-in. Written decision at day 30.

We hire off the test and the trial, not the interview. If you are the kind of strategist who would rather prove it than pitch it, apply.

Job Description

Tempo is seeking a highly motivated and skilled Engineering Technician with strong welding capabilities to produce engineered parts and assemble testing apparatus, instruments, sensors, prototypes, and power electronic components. The ideal candidate is a driven professional who has recently graduated from a strong technical program, has 2–4 years of hands-on experience, and is eager to bring their energy and foundational skills to a fast-paced startup environment. You will work both independently and collaboratively to bring our engineering designs to life. This role is integral to the development and refinement of high-temperature energy storage components, offering an incredible opportunity to work on complex R&D projects and grow your career at the cutting edge of thermochemical energy storage technology.

Key Responsibilities

  • Interpret 3D CAD models, 2D drawings, and spec charts to plan and execute part manufacturing; measure, mark, and cut raw materials accordingly
  • Perform TIG/MIG welding on structural assemblies and operate machine shop equipment (mills, lathes, drill presses, band saws) to create or modify parts
  • Assist in assembling complex mechanical and electromechanical systems as required
  • Prepare finished components for dimensional accuracy, weld integrity, and defects for inspection
  • Modify and repair parts, prototypes, and test rigs to support agile R&D needs using welding, grinding, cutting, and machining techniques
  • Work with high-temperature and specialty materials (refractory metals, ceramics, alloys) to meet durability and performance requirements for thermochemical applications
  • Partner with engineers to interpret technical drawings, troubleshoot fabrication challenges, and recommend design improvements for manufacturability
  • Inspect fabricated and welded components for structural integrity, finish, and dimensional accuracy to ensure parts meet required tolerances
  • Maintain welding gear and machine tools in optimal working condition; follow all safety protocols when welding, handling high-temperature materials, and operating machinery
  • Record prototype builds, assembly procedures, fabrication parameters, and component modifications, providing real-time feedback to engineering and R&D teams

Qualifications
Required:

  • Associate degree in Mechanical Engineering Technology, formal welding certification, or completion of a technical/trade school program
  • 2–4 years of hands-on experience in mechanical fabrication, welding, and assembly; experience in an R&D or startup environment a plus
  • Proficiency in TIG and MIG welding on various metals
  • Exceptional safety acumen and commitment to safe work practices
  • Familiarity with manual mills, lathes, grinders, and general metalworking tools
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and technical specifications
  • Strong willingness to learn about high-temperature and specialty materials (ceramics, alloys, refractory metals) 
  • Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to work to tight tolerances
  • Proactive learner with the ability to assist in troubleshooting basic fabrication challenges.
  • Clear communicator able to collaborate effectively with engineers and team members in a fast-paced R&D environment
  • Genuine interest in learning and growing within an R&D or startup environment; comfortable wearing multiple hats to get the job done

Preferred:

  • Experience in high-temperature applications, thermal systems, or energy storage
  • Knowledge of materials science, particularly around fabrication and welding of heat-resistant materials
  • Familiarity with safety standards and best practices in fabrication and high-temperature R&D settings

Compensation Range

The US base hourly salary range for this full-time position is $24.27 to $30.76 + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, location, and relevant education or training. 

Please note that the compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include equity or benefits.

Working at Tempo

Tempo is a lean organization working on exciting challenges, and the people who thrive here share a few things in common beyond their technical skills.

  • Clear, direct communication: You professionally say what you mean, lead with empathy, use tact, ask when you're unsure, and keep the people around you informed without being asked. At a company our size, communication gaps are expensive, and good communicators add to success and efficiency!
  • Low-ego helpfulness: You're willing to jump in on work that isn't strictly yours, whether that's helping a teammate debug something, lending a hand in the shop, or flagging an issue you noticed outside your lane. No one here succeeds in a silo.
  • Intellectual curiosity: You're genuinely interested in how things work, not just your piece of it, but the broader system. Tempo sits at the intersection of chemistry, mechanical engineering, power electronics, and software; the more you understand about the whole, the more valuable you become.
  • Business awareness: You understand that your work exists in a business context. You think about cost, timeline, and tradeoffs—not just technical elegance—and you make decisions accordingly.
  • Comfort with ambiguity: Processes here are still being built. You can make progress without a perfect playbook, and you know when to ask for direction versus when to use your judgment and move forward.
  • Accountability: You own your outcomes, including the misses. When something goes sideways, the instinct here is to fix it and learn from it, not to explain why it wasn't your fault.

The role: Senior Product Manager, Developer Experience

You'll own the experience of developers who build, test, and deploy AI agents with Trase. Your job is to help a new developer get to a working agent quickly and give experienced teams tools they can trust in production. As teams move from experimental agent demos to mission-critical production systems, you will define the standard for how serious developers build, evaluate, and ship AI agents.

You’ll be the product manager for Trase Arena, our SDK and tools for building AI agents. Your scope covers a developer’s work from the first build through deployment, observability and improvement on Origin. You'll work directly with developers, engineering, design, and product marketing to build an experience that earns adoption through the product itself.

  • Know the developer: Work directly with developers to understand what they're trying to build. Observe where they get stuck, test assumptions, and use what you learn to set priorities.
  • Set a high bar for the tools: Own the developer experience across the SDK, APIs, and CLI. Make them consistent, predictable, well documented, and useful for real development work.

About the role:

Curri is hiring its first dedicated Senior Security Engineer to join the Foundations team, which owns security, infrastructure, DevOps, and our AI engineering platform. This is a builder role, not a monitoring role: you'll own security across our applications, cloud, and AI agents, write the tooling and guardrails that make the secure path the easy path, and be the person engineers, leadership, and customers trust to make the call on risk. As the first hire into this role, you'll shape how security works at Curri for years to come.

What you will do:

 - Own application and cloud security end to end: threat modeling, secure design reviews, and hands-on work on sensitive code paths across our TypeScript/Node GraphQL API, React and React Native apps, Go services, and AWS/EKS infrastructure defined in Pulumi.

 - Build internal security tooling and guardrails instead of gates, such as authentication services, access proxies, secrets handling, policy-as-code, and CI checks that developers barely notice until they save them.

 - Secure our AI-forward engineering platform. Curri runs autonomous agents that review, write, and deploy code; you'll own their access boundaries, credential handling, prompt-injection defenses, and audit trail, along with the policies for how staff use AI tools.

 - Turn our security scanning (SAST, secrets, container, and IaC) into a program with signal: tune it, triage it, and drive findings to closure against clear SLAs.

 - Stand up detection and response: build high-signal alerting across cloud, identity, and application logs, lead security incidents, and make sure postmortem follow-through actually happens.

 - Run the vulnerability lifecycle: scope and manage external penetration tests, validate and prioritize findings, partner with teams on fixes, and verify closure.

 - Partner on compliance and customer trust: help run our SOC 2 program, answer enterprise security reviews, and turn what customers ask for into program improvements, not just questionnaire answers.

 - Raise the security bar of the whole engineering team by mentoring engineers on secure design patterns, especially authorization, identity, and multi-tenant data isolation, and making security a normal part of how we ship.

 - Communicate risk clearly to engineers, executives, and customers in the terms that matter to each, and help shape the security roadmap as the function grows.

What you need to have:

 - 8+ years of professional experience in software engineering and/or security, including at least 3 years focused on application, product, or cloud security.

 - A track record of designing and building secure web applications, APIs, and internal tools. You read and write production code and are credible in a code review.

 - Deep, hands-on knowledge of web and API vulnerabilities, especially authorization flaws (IDOR/BOLA), authentication and SSO (SAML, OIDC, JWT), SSRF, and injection, and how to find and fix them at scale.

 - Strong cloud security experience in AWS and Kubernetes: IAM, network segmentation, workload isolation, secrets management, and infrastructure as code.

 - Experience leading security incidents, ideally as the person in charge, with calm, diligent response and clear communication.

 - The ability to work as a team of one: you prioritize by real risk, make pragmatic tradeoffs, and ship without a playbook handed to you.

 - Fluency with AI-paired delivery (Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent), and a clear view of the new risks AI agents and LLM-integrated apps introduce.

 - Strong, direct communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and empathy for the developers and customers you're protecting.

Bonus points for:

 - Being an early or first security hire at a startup, and being able to speak to what you built first and why.

 - Detection engineering experience implementing and maintaining a SIEM or detection-as-code pipeline.

 - Securing LLM applications or agentic systems, including familiarity with the OWASP LLM/Agentic Top 10, MCP, or AI governance frameworks like NIST AI RMF.

 - Experience with SOC 2, ISO 27001, or enterprise customer security reviews.

 - Proven offensive skills, such as pentesting, bug bounty, or CTFs, used to assess real-world exploitability.

 - Experience with our stack: TypeScript, Node, GraphQL, Postgres, Go, EKS, Pulumi, NATS.

 - Contributions to the security community through research, talks, open source, or writing.

What is in it for you?

 - The chance to build Curri's security function from the ground up, with direct access to leadership and real authority over how we manage risk.

 - Hard, interesting problems: multi-tenant logistics data, enterprise SSO, a large GraphQL surface, and an AI agent platform that ships code to production.

 - A genuinely AI-forward engineering culture where Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and Bedrock are in daily use.

 - Competitive salary, equity compensation, and comprehensive benefits (health, dental, vision, 401K).

Who are we?

We are Curri, and our mission is to build the network and software that move the world’s goods with speed, intelligence, and trust. Curri provides on-demand, last-mile logistics for construction and adjacent industries with our nationwide fleet of cars, trucks, and flatbeds.
Founded in 2018 and part of the YC S19 Batch, we’re solving the massive inefficiencies that exist in the construction industry. Our headquarters are in Ventura, CA. Learn more at curri.com http://curri.com.



Curri is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment. We don't discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and businesses with fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and transparent financial services products. Coast’s mission is to deliver this at a transformational scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card built on a cutting-edge spend management platform.

Coast builds payments and spend management for fleet businesses: fuel cards, corporate cards and bill pay. We’re becoming AI-native: AI handles the repeatable work, so people can focus on customers and the hardest problems.

Our sales team already runs on AI workflows we built in-house. Now we're building a small internal AI team to take that across the whole company. You'll join as one of two AI Operations Engineers, reporting to our AI Lead.

About the Role

This is a builder role with an operator’s mindset. You’ll find the highest-leverage work across Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Support, Finance, Risk, Product, and Operations, and own it end to end, from first conversation to production. Some weeks you’ll write code; others you’ll run a workshop or redesign a process with a team.

Everyone at Coast uses Claude and builds their own skills. You build what they can’t: autonomous agents, and the foundation that makes everyone’s skills better.

In your first six months, you’ll ship three or more agents that teams rely on daily, each backed by evals that show it improving month over month. You’ll drive measurable gains in Coast’s operating efficiency, tracked in hours saved.

What You’ll Do

  • Find and prioritize the work. Sit with teams, map their workflows, and size the time saved. Turn what you find into a ranked backlog with the AI Lead.
  • Build autonomous agents. Ship event-driven agents that do multi-step work across our stack. You’ll own the engineering off-the-shelf tools can’t do:
    • Loop and orchestration: design agent loops, sub-agent handoffs, and when to act alone or escalate to a human.
    • Memory and context: model shared memory as a knowledge graph, and decide what each agent sees, remembers and forgets.
    • Custom tooling: build the tools our agents need.
    • Traces and evals: trace every run, score outputs against test sets built from real outcomes, and prove each version beats the last.
  • Measure impact. Define success metrics for each build, track adoption and time saved, and report results to leadership.
  • Run what you ship. Own reliability, latency and cost in production, and catch regressions before users do. Partner with Security and IT on access, audit trails and the handling of sensitive data.
  • Enable the company. An AI-native company runs on self-service, and self-service needs solid infrastructure. You’ll architect the shared foundation the rest of Coast builds on: knowledge bases, application databases, templates, tools, and connectors. Then you’ll help people use it through training, office hours and hackathons, and grow a network of AI champions.
  • Stay on the cutting edge. Try new models and tools as they land, measure them against what we run today, and keep raising the bar on everything you’ve built.

Projects you might take on

  • Autonomous product help docs. Build a brain that captures questions from customers (support tickets and calls) and employees (Slack). It spots missing or outdated articles, drafts updates, sends them for review, and learns from what gets approved and shared with customers.
  • Deal coach for large trials. Build an agent that creates value calculators and tailored pitch decks from call transcripts and account data. It coaches AEs and CSMs through each trial with next steps, and learns which plays win.

Requirements

  • 2–5 years in operations, product, solutions or forward-deployed engineering, internal tools, or a similar role at a fast-moving company.
  • A track record of shipping AI workflows or automations that people use every day. Show us what you built.
  • Hands-on fluency with Claude Code, Cursor or similar coding agents, plus LLM tooling such as prompt design, tool use and MCP.
  • You've built at least one agent with persistent memory or a feedback loop that made it better over time.
  • Experience with evals: building test sets, scoring outputs and using the results to improve an agent.
  • Comfort writing and reading code: SQL, plus Python or TypeScript scripting, APIs and webhooks.
  • Clear communication with non-technical teammates. You can teach as well as build.
  • High agency: you spot inefficient processes and fix them without waiting to be asked.

Nice to have

  • A software engineering background.
  • Experience building with the MCP servers or APIs for tools like Salesforce, Notion, Slack and Gmail.
  • Experience with guardrails or monitoring for AI systems.
  • Background in fintech, payments or another regulated industry.
  • Startup experience, especially at an AI-native company.

Compensation and Benefits

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of our total compensation package that also includes benefits and equity. Pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including scope and qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to other Coast employees. We expect the majority of candidates who are offered roles at Coast to fall healthily within the range based on these factors.

Salary range: $150,000 - $180,000 annually

Equity Grant: Meaningful potential upside given Coast’s early-stage trajectory

Benefits Overview:

  • Medical, dental and vision insurance
  • Flexible paid time off (vacation, personal well being, paid holidays)
  • Tools to help manage your financial wellness, including webinars, access to an equity tax advisory service, and company-sponsored 401(k)
  • Paid parental leave
  • $400 accessories allowance (a keyboard, mouse, headphones, etc.)
  • Education stipend
  • Free lunch every Friday

Coast is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are building a diverse and inclusive environment, so we encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. Hi 👋🏻 I’m Louis, Head of Security. You’ll report directly to me.

What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you contribute to useful projects, make practical decisions, and work in an almost-no-meeting culture. The product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: tens of thousands of daily users who depend on our software, and customers whose trust your work will help us earn.

We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet.

You’ll join our Security team, a single team with multiple specializations overseeing security across the business. I report to Abhik, our Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re bubbling with ideas on how to support Talent Acquisition through software, and we’ve started the journey of building products beyond Talent Acquisition. We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner).




ROLE OVERVIEW

We’re looking for an engineer with a passion to learn whose focus is on building “paved roads” specifically around making secure delivery part of the way we build and ship software. You’ll operate the checks and workflows around our delivery pipeline, help engineers act on useful findings, and make routine exceptions straightforward under agreed policies.

We expect you to bring the same care to the reliability of a security check and the time it costs an engineer as you bring to the risk it addresses. You’ll build the integrations, learn from rollout, and maintain what you ship.

We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, over 2500 customers, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet, but you now probably have a good idea as to why we're hiring for this role 😅.




ABOUT THE ROLE AND HOW WE WORK

We’re also advertising this opening as Senior Security Platform Engineer - Secure Delivery. Both titles describe the same position; please apply once using the title that best reflects your experience.

Your mission is to make our delivery pipeline secure by default across application code, infrastructure, dependencies, containers, and product configuration. You’ll own the technical implementation and operation of delivery-security tooling and controls, including integration, configuration, tuning, reliability, and coverage.

Product Engineering teams own triage and remediation for the features they maintain. Application Security provides specialist analysis and defines product-security test requirements. Infrastructure retains ownership of the underlying cloud platform. You’ll work with those teams to make agreed checks and policies run reliably in the delivery workflow.

In practice, you’ll:

 - Deploy, configure, integrate, and tune static analysis, dependency, secret, container, and Infrastructure as Code scanning in our CI/CD workflows.

 - Inventory production repositories and delivery paths, including prompts and model configuration. Make scanner coverage distinct from application-specific tests of AI behavior; AppSec defines those tests, and you operate agreed delivery checks.

 - Start new checks in report-only mode where appropriate, then implement agreed warn and block policies using exploitability, exposure, and compensating controls.

 - Give engineers self-service exceptions within documented rules, with an owner, justification, expiry, and audit trail. Escalate decisions outside those rules to Security leadership with the relevant specialist analysis.

 - Build automation and AI-assisted workflows that enrich findings, propose fixes, and support Product Engineering’s triage under documented criteria. Preserve required checks, review, and rollback for automated patch changes.

 - Make coverage, integration failures, finding age by risk, time to triage and remediate, false blocks, build delay, and bypasses visible. Record mitigations separately from completed fixes and connect useful telemetry to GRC evidence.

 - Work with Infrastructure on cloud-posture monitoring, useful critical-misconfiguration alerts, and bounded remediation automation.

 - Extend into shared-image hardening and artifact provenance as the delivery foundations mature.

To ground it with examples, you could:

 - Roll out secret scanning with push protection and make a blocked push understandable and actionable for an engineer.

 - Turn a repeated scanner-exception request into a PR workflow with a reason, expiry, and evidence for revisiting it.

 - Reproduce a dependency issue in the application, add a regression check, and build a workflow that proposes a patch with useful evidence.

 - Show which delivery paths are covered, where checks fail, and whether enforcement is addressing risk while keeping build delays reasonable.




WHY YOU SHOULD AND SHOULDN’T APPLY

You’ve built and operated CI/CD, developer tooling, or infrastructure automation used by other engineers. You can write maintainable code, explain the failure modes of what you shipped, and use security evidence to make a practical rollout decision. Supply-chain and scanner experience is useful; you can learn individual tools as part of the work.

You’ve applied AI in engineering and can explain how you check its outputs and permissions. You enjoy treating engineers as users, making build-versus-buy decisions, and improving adoption and reliability after launch.

You might not enjoy the role if:

 - You prefer to deliver a prototype and hand off its operation. Reliability, tuning, and existing integrations are part of the work.

 - You prefer a prescribed backlog to investigating an ambiguous problem, writing a proposal, and bringing partners into the work.

 - You want standalone assessments to be your main output. This role centers on working delivery capabilities and their adoption.
   


INTERVIEW PROCESS

If this also sounds exciting to you, please apply. We review every application and aim to get back to candidates within 2-3 days. For candidates who advance to the interview process, here is what you can expect:

 - Recruiter Screen - 30 mins

 - Hiring Manager Intro Call - 20 mins

 - Past Projects Deep Dive - 45 mins

 - Founder Screening - 45 mins

 - Take-Home Assessment +  Practical Assessment Review - 1 hr (2-3 spent on take-home assignment)

 - Cross-Functional Stakeholder Interview - 45 mins




ROLE-SPECIFIC TECHNOLOGY AND TOOLS

For this role, CI/CD and infrastructure automation experience matter more than familiarity with a particular scanner. GitHub Actions or comparable systems, Terraform, containers, and cloud controls are relevant. You should be comfortable writing production automation in TypeScript, Python, Go, or a comparable language. Tool choices and individual scanner integrations are part of the work.




YOUR FIRST THREE MONTHS AT ASHBY

Your early changes will give you a tour of our codebase, infrastructure, and best practices, increasing in scope and ambiguity as you learn how we work. You’ll pair program with your onboarding peer as you learn the delivery workflows.

Your initial focus will be to:

 - Map production delivery paths and gaps across code, infrastructure, prompts, configuration, and evals, with clear ownership of the different checks.

 - Deliver a bounded scanning integration, such as secret push protection or report-only static analysis, with a usable finding workflow.

 - Establish initial warn, block, and self-service exception rules with the relevant partners and make Product Engineering ownership visible.

 - Baseline coverage, integration failures, false blocks, and build delay so the next rollout has evidence to build on.

Early progress means engineers can use the selected checks, act on their findings, and handle routine exceptions. Broader rollout follows the agreed risk policy and what the first integration teaches us.




BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

 - A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. The actual number may increase to satisfy local requirements.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.




CLOSING

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Role Overview:

As a Senior Production Engineer, you will play a key role in maintaining the reliability and stability of CoreWeave’s cloud infrastructure. You will work closely with the Production Engineer Team Lead and other engineers to support incident response, platform reliability, and operational improvements. This position is ideal for individuals eager to grow their technical skills, contribute to a high-performing team, and make an impact on the operational excellence of CoreWeave’s cloud services.

Incident Management & Support:

  • Assist in incident response efforts by helping identify and resolve service disruptions quickly, working under the guidance of more senior engineers.

  • Contribute to the development and maintenance of incident response playbooks to ensure preparedness for various failure scenarios.
  • Participate in communication efforts during incidents, updating stakeholders and keeping clear records of incident activities.

Operational Support & Reliability:

  • Monitor system performance and health using tools like Prometheus and Grafana, identifying any performance issues or potential incidents.
  • Help implement automation and process improvements to enhance efficiency and reduce manual intervention in incident detection and recovery.
  • Support the development of KPIs and SLAs for incident management and ensure alignment with team goals.
  • Collaborate with engineers across teams to improve platform reliability, resilience improvements, and disaster recovery.

Team Collaboration & Development:

  • Work closely with other engineers to troubleshoot system issues, refine workflows, and support ongoing operational needs.

 - Run technical discovery. With Sales and Engineering, map a staff's current workflow and pain points, specifically focusing on their technical constraints: networks, hosting, identity, and integration requirements, especially in multi-network environments.

 - Support accreditation. Help create and review security documentation, including STIG checklists and ATO artifacts, alongside our cybersecurity team so deployments are accredited on the customer's timeline.

 - Align stakeholders. Get technical stakeholders on both sides to agree on requirements, constraints, and tradeoffs, so customers see value sooner. Ensure those technical requirements are properly translated into contract deliverables.

 - Scope integrations. Design how Onebrief Connect fits into a command's ecosystem: APIs, data pipelines, Foundry and Maven Smart System, CUOPS tools, and dashboards.

 - Deliver tailored demos.  Lead technical demonstrations and solution validation, partnering with Sales and customer-facing teams to demonstrate Onebrief's technical capabilities, deployment architecture, security posture, and integration options.

 - Run pilot deployments. Configure Onebrief in new and untested environments to enable limited uses in support of new sales.

 - Turn field experience into patterns. Convert what you learn in deployments into structured workflows and reusable implementation patterns, and feed clear requirements to Product and Engineering.

 - Work with customers onsite. This is a hybrid role, requiring you to work alongside customers as necessary.

 - Secret Clearance required.

 - Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

 - 4+ years in solutions engineering, infrastructure or deployment engineering, or forward-deployed engineering, working closely with go-to-market and operational teams

 - Strong expertise with containers (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes)

 - Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and on-premises virtualization (RHEL)

 - Solid understanding of networking concepts and protocols, and of security best practices for highly sensitive environments

 - Strong presence with customers, from action officers to senior leaders, and clear, concise writing

Why this role matters:

As a Software Engineer, you’ll help build and run the platform that every ICEYE image passes through before a customer sees it. The SAR Processing Platform validates raw radar data, decides when and where to process it, runs the processing workflows, catalogs the products and gates their delivery. You’ll join a small team that owns this orchestration layer end to end, covering how incoming data is validated, scheduled and processed, how products are cataloged and delivered, and the tools operators use to run it. The platform runs in the cloud and on on-premises clusters at customer sites, and you’ll work daily with SAR processing engineers, other engineering teams across the platform, DevOps, product and delivery.

Who We Are

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world’s largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

Your day-to-day responsibilities

 - Build and maintain the backend services that schedule, process and catalog satellite data

 - Write and tune the processing workflows: resource sizing, reliability and integration of new processor versions

 - Keep production healthy: debug failed or stuck jobs from logs, metrics and the database, and turn recurring incidents into fixes or tooling

 - Ship through automated, version-controlled deployments to test, staging, production and on-prem environments, and roll out new processor versions and products with the SAR processing engineers using gradual rollouts and quality gates

 - Write tests, documentation and runbooks, and review teammates’ code

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

 - 2 to 5 years of backend software engineering experience, with solid Go and working Python, and willingness to read and occasionally change Rust

 - Hands-on Kubernetes and Docker as a developer: you have deployed, debugged and sized workloads yourself, not only used a cluster someone else ran

 - PostgreSQL (schema design, migrations, query debugging) and AWS fundamentals (S3, IAM, EKS or equivalent)

 - Experience running software in production, including incident debugging and postmortems

 - Pragmatic use of AI/LLM tools in daily development, fluent English, and comfort asking and answering questions in a distributed team

Nice to haves:

 - Argo Workflows, Airflow or similar; NATS or Kafka; any Rust experience

 - Geospatial or remote-sensing data (GeoTIFF, COG, STAC, GDAL), or any large-file scientific data pipeline

 - Helm, Flux, Terraform; Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry

Application Process

 1. Recruiter Interview (30 mins online)

 2. Hiring Manager Interview (60 mins online)

 3. Technical Interview/ Task ( 60- 90 mins)

 4. Onsite/ Final Interview (60 mins)
    
    

Working at ICEYE

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.

How We Work (Our Values)

Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.

Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

Have fun: What we do matters, and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing, at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.

We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us, and we’ll do our best to help.

Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com http://iceye.com.

You’ll join a small team that owns this orchestration layer end to end, running in the cloud and on on-premises clusters at customer sites, and you’ll help decide where it goes next. The hard problems are scheduling and routing under cost and latency constraints, data integrity across a multi-step pipeline, safe rollouts across many environments, and keeping a system that processes every ICEYE image reliable with a small team.

Who We Are

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world’s largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

 - Own the design of the orchestration layer (scheduling rules, routing between processors, failure handling and resource planning) and build and maintain the backend services and processing workflows behind it. Write the design, argue it with production data, and land it in stages.

 - Lead incident response for processing incidents, run cross-team root-cause work with the SAR processing and other engineering teams, and make sure postmortem actions close.

 - Drive platform-wide changes across repositories and environments: multi-release rollouts across cloud and on-prem clusters, migrations that never lose data on first rollout, gradual rollouts and quality gates. Harden access to the platform with least-privilege access to data stores, audit logging across services, and access reviews with Security Engineering.

 - Review designs and code, pair on hard debugging, and raise the bar on tests, documentation and runbooks. Represent the platform toward SAR processing, other engineering teams, product, DevOps and on-prem customers: turn requests into prioritized work with a business case, and push back with data when needed.

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

 - 5+ years of backend software engineering, including building and operating distributed systems in production, with strong Go plus strong Python or Rust

 - Deep hands-on Kubernetes experience (resource management, scheduling, node pools and autoscaling, Helm), plus AWS (S3, IAM, EKS) and Terraform

 - PostgreSQL at depth (performance, zero-downtime migrations, query design) and experience with event-driven and batch pipelines: idempotency, at-least-once delivery, backpressure, large objects in S3

 - A track record of running production (incident lead, reliability improvements you can quantify) and strong written design communication: you can lay out options, back a choice with data and get a team to agree. Fluent English, a collaborative mindset in a distributed team, and pragmatic use of AI/LLM tools in daily development

 - Geospatial or remote-sensing data (GeoTIFF, COG, STAC, GDAL), or SAR specifically; on-premises Kubernetes (RKE2 or similar) and restricted deployments

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're expanding our protein expression into mammalian cell culture, for example in CHO and HEK cells. Our mammalian expression volume is growing fast. We're looking for a Cell Culture Engineer who has spent years growing and transfecting mammalian cells and knows what to do when a run goes wrong.

You'll work alongside our production and mammalian cell teams as a hands-on expert in the cell culture lab. You'll keep cultures healthy and on schedule, run transfections and expressions, and be the person the team turns to when yields drop or cells misbehave. This is a hands-on role, not a management role.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run mammalian expression. Maintain, expand, and passage cell lines, and run transfections and expressions on a production schedule.

 - Troubleshoot. When viability, growth, or yield falls off, find the cause and fix it.

 - Own the cell bank. Thaw, freeze, and track cell stocks, and protect the lines from contamination and drift.

 - Optimize conditions. Test culture and transfection conditions, and turn what works into the standard protocol.

 - Scale with automation. Work with our automation team to move cell handling onto liquid handlers as volume grows.

 - Hand off clean material. Deliver harvests ready for purification and downstream assays.

 - Keep the lab running. Look after incubators, biosafety cabinets, and cell counters, and keep the BSL-2 space organized and compliant.

 - Write SOPs and train. Document protocols that others can follow, and train the team on aseptic technique and our cell culture workflows.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Extensive hands-on experience with common mammalian model cell lines, for example CHO and HEK, including transfection and expression.

 - BSc / MSc in biotechnology, cell biology, or a relevant field.

 - A troubleshooting track record. You've rescued failing cultures and expressions and can explain what went wrong and why.

 - Flawless aseptic technique and experience working under BSL-2 conditions.

 - Experience with high-throughput formats: multi-well plates and many conditions in parallel, not only flasks.

 - Experience with liquid handlers is a plus.

 - Experience with antibody or Fc-fusion production is a plus.

 - Organized and precise. You track every stock, passage, and transfection, and you follow protocols exactly.

 - You use AI tools effectively and with discernment. We use them across the company and expect you to check, edit, and stand behind what they produce, not pass along unreviewed output.

 - Comfortable in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift. Cells don't keep office hours, so you plan around them.

Our Ethos

We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

About the role

Rain builds payments and stablecoin infrastructure. Finance, Risk, Compliance, and our partners rely on data from card transactions, settlements, ledger entries, and onchain transfers.

We’re looking for a Data Engineer with batch and streaming experience to bring this data into our warehouse and keep it correct. You’ll build scalable, idempotent pipelines that handle late and duplicate data and alert us when something breaks.

At Rain, everyone models data, writes production-quality code, and automates their own workflows. We use AI to speed up repetitive work, but we own and check the results. In this role, you’ll automate ingestion and quality checks so new sources come online quickly and stay trustworthy.

What you’ll do

 - Build scalable batch and streaming pipelines, choosing the right approach for latency, cost, and correctness.

 - Process events near real time, handling deduplication, windowing, and late or out-of-order events.

 - Own batch ingestion from databases (CDC), files (SFTP and GCS), APIs, and onchain sources.

 - Build incremental dbt models that handle late data, duplicates, CDC deletes, and backfills; reconcile streaming and batch outputs.

 - Orchestrate pipelines in Dagster with sensors, schedules, and alerts.

 - Add freshness, volume, and reconciliation checks to every source, and fix root causes.

 - Work with backend pods on event and table contracts to prevent downstream breakage.

 - Partner with Analytics Engineers, Data Scientists, and Risk on their data needs, including ML features.

What you’ll need

 - At least 3 years building production data solutions, including owning both batch and streaming pipelines end to end, from source to warehouse.

 - Experience designing data solutions at scale.

 - Strong SQL and Python / Rust, plus experience with a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, ClickHouse, or Snowflake and an understanding of their trade-offs.

 - Streaming experience with tools such as Pub/Sub, Kafka, Dataflow/Beam, or Flink.

 - Batch experience with dbt and an orchestrator such as Dagster or Airflow.

 - Experience with production data quality testing, monitoring, and reconciliation.

 - Ability to debug across the source database, pipeline, warehouse, and report.

 - Ability to use AI tools to learn and work faster while checking their output.

Nice to have

 - Building offline and real-time ML feature pipelines, such as fraud or risk features.

 - Working with payments, banking, or blockchain data, including EVM or Solana events and indexers.

 - Using CDC and ingestion tools such as Datastream, Debezium, Meltano, Fivetran, or Airbyte.

 - Experience with GCP.

We build software products that turn ICEYE’s satellite data and analytics into outcomes customers can rely on during real events such as floods, wildfires, and earthquakes.

This is an individual contributor role where you are expected to take ownership of your work and help deliver end-to-end product slices across backend and frontend. You help us ship frequently, keep systems supportable in production, and continuously reduce friction in how we build and run our products.


Who We Are

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy – day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring (including oil-spill detection), and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.

ICEYE is headquartered in Finland and operates globally across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We have more than 900 employees, united by a shared vision: improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.




Your day-to day responsibilities


 - End-to-End Delivery: Own full product slices by building seamless functionality from backend APIs to frontend UIs, turning vague requirements into testable, production-ready code.

 - Operational Excellence: Maintain system reliability by participating in on-call rotations and improving "observability" through meaningful alerts, clear logs, and automated runbooks.

 - Process Optimization: Boost team velocity by identifying delivery bottlenecks such as slow CI or flaky tests, and automating away recurring toil to focus on novel engineering challenges.

 - Pragmatic Engineering: Design simple, maintainable architectures that prioritize incremental changes, clear documentation, and high-quality code reviews to ensure safe deployments.

 - Collaborative Leadership: Align with cross-functional partners (Product, Design, Data) to solve problems while mentoring peers through pair programming and shared technical context.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves

 - Experience building and maintaining production software in a cloud environment, across both backend and frontend.

 - Solid proficiency in at least one backend language (for example Python, TypeScript/Node.js, Go, Java or Kotlin) and one modern frontend framework (for example React, Vue or Angular).

 - Comfortable designing and consuming APIs, and working with relational and/or NoSQL databases.

 - Writes automated tests and keeps changes small and reviewable; ships, learns and iterates.

 - Builds with operations in mind: resilience, debuggability and supportability.

 - Extensive experience with Docker in development and production environments.

 - Communicates clearly: can explain trade-offs and align with Product and peers.

 - Uses AI-assisted tools (for example Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude Code) pragmatically, with good habits for verifying output.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with Python (especially FastAPI and async patterns) and/or TypeScript with React.

 - Familiarity with geospatial domains, remote sensing or data-intensive applications.

 - Experience with event-driven architecture and distributed systems.

 - Familiarity with Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code (for example Terraform).

 - Exposure to regulated data environments (for example ISO 27001, DORA or GDPR).

 - Experience improving the structure, performance or maintainability of a growing frontend codebase.




APPLICATION PROCESS

 - TA Interview

 - Hiring Manager Interview

 - Take Home Task

 - Panel Interview

 - Department Lead Interview

 - Final Interview with SVP of Solutions



Working at ICEYE

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.



How We Work (Our Values)

Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.

 - Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

 - See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

 - Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

 - Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

 - Have fun: What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.
   
   

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing, at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.



Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.

We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us—we’ll do our best to help.

Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at www.iceye.com http://www.iceye.com. https://www.iceye.com/

Clara is the leading platform in Latin America for companies to execute and manage every payment operation. More than 50,000 leading and fast-growing businesses run on our corporate cards, bill pay, financing and B2B payments, and in 2025 the Financial Times named Clara the region’s fastest-growing company. We’re passionate about helping every company we work with become more effective—and, through that, raising the region’s competitiveness. We’re ~400 people, backed by Notable Capital, Coatue, Kaszek, monashees, DST Global, ICONIQ, General Catalyst and Goldman Sachs, among others.

What you'll do

This is a highly hands-on design role at the intersection of growth, performance marketing, and AI. You will design the assets and experiences that drive Clara's acquisition engine across Mexico, Brazil, and Colombia — ad creatives, landing pages, lifecycle journeys, and conversion flows — using AI tools as a core part of your daily workflow, from first prompt to final asset. You'll help define what AI-augmented growth design looks like at scale, on a team that is actively building AI-native workflows into everything we do.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Design and produce performance creative at scale — static ads, video concepts, carousels, and social assets for Meta, Google, and LinkedIn — using AI tools (e.g. Midjourney, Ideogram, Runway, Figma AI) combined with strong design craft.
  • Design and optimize landing pages and conversion flows, applying CRO best practices for hierarchy, scroll depth, and clarity — and partnering with the Paid Media team to A/B test and iterate until the metrics move.
  • Use AI daily to accelerate creative production: generating visual variants, exploring concepts, drafting layouts, and turning briefs into testable assets in hours, not weeks.
  • Build and maintain a scalable creative system — templates, components, and brand-consistent asset libraries in Figma — so the Growth team ships faster across 3 markets and 3 languages (PT-BR, ES-MX, ES-CO).
  • Partner with Growth - Paid Media to interpret creative performance data, generate hypotheses, and feed learnings back into the next iteration.
  • Run visual QA on assets and pages before they go live; keep the brand consistent across every touchpoint of the funnel.
  • Scout, pilot, and adopt new AI design tools — you keep our creative stack ahead of the industry, and document workflows so the whole team levels up.
  • Use automation tools (e.g. n8n, Make, Zapier) to reduce repetitive production work and create scalable creative workflows.

Who you are:

Must haves:

  • 2+ years of experience in growth design, performance/marketing design with measurable business impact.
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating ad creatives, landing pages, or conversion-focused work — applications without a portfolio will not be considered.
  • Active, daily user of AI tools — generative image/video tools (Midjourney, Ideogram, Runway or similar) and LLMs (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) are part of your real workflow, not an occasional experiment.
  • Can write effective prompts: you know how to give AI models context, constraints, and references to get useful outputs on the first or second try — and you know when to take over and finish by hand.
  • Expert in Figma; you think in components and systems, not one-offs.
  • Conversion mindset — you track CTR, CVR, and CAC the way other designers track likes, and you use data to inform design decisions.
  • Comfortable working with experimentation: A/B tests, creative testing frameworks, iterating based on results.
  • Organized and able to handle multiple markets and formats in parallel.
  • Comfortable communicating with both creative and analytical teams.

Nice to haves:

  • Experience with motion design (After Effects, Lottie, or AI-powered video tools).
  • Experience building landing pages hands-on (Webflow, Framer, or similar).
  • Experience with automation tools like n8n, Make, or Zapier to build creative production workflows.
  • Experience building custom GPTs, AI agents, or AI-assisted creative pipelines.
  • Familiarity with GA4, Mixpanel, or attribution tools for creative performance analysis.
  • Experience designing for multi-market or multi-language portfolios.
  • Experience working with B2B SaaS or Fintech.
  • Basic understanding of front-end (HTML/CSS) or vibe-coding tools (Lovable, v0, Replit).

Where we work

This is a hybrid role: you'll split your time between the office, customers and home. We don't set a minimum number of office days for most roles — you'll spend time in the office naturally, and most days during your ramp-up or when your leader asks.

Why Clara

  • A high talent-density team driven to make an impact in Latin America — low ego, high ownership.
  • Competitive salary and stock options (ESOP) from day one.
  • An annual learning budget and accelerated development paths.
  • English is our working language, with Spanish and Portuguese every day.

How we work

  • Clarity — Open and direct communication: we say what we mean and give context where it matters.
  • Simplicity — If it can be simpler, it should be.
  • Ownership — We own everything we do, end to end. When something needs to happen, we don't wait.
  • Pride — We hold ourselves to a high standard, and it shows in what we deliver.
  • ABC (Always Be Changing) — We adapt fast, embrace change, and keep learning.
  • Inclusivity — Diverse ideas, stories and perspectives build a better Clara.

If you meet the must-haves, apply — the nice-to-haves are a bonus, not a requirement.

As a Senior Infrastructure/SRE Engineer on the Convert pillar, you'll:

 - Build and maintain our infrastructure-as-code foundation in Pulumi, and evolve the patterns and shared components other teams build on.

 - Improve scalability and reliability of distributed, event-driven systems, including our Druid, MongoDB, and Airflow workloads, with a focus on low latency.

 - Make observability the foundation of how we operate. Improve the dashboards, alerts, and SLOs for the systems you own so we catch issues before customers notice, and on-call pages are actionable instead of noisy.

 - BA/BS degree or equivalent experience

 - Business-level fluency to read, write and speak in English

 - Have 5+ years owning and operating cloud infrastructure in a customer-facing environment with little tolerance for downtime. You come from infrastructure, SRE, or cloud engineering with a love of automation and code, or from software engineering with a deep interest in cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.

 - Have deep hands-on experience with AWS and a clear view of what good cloud operations look like.

 - Have used infrastructure as code (Pulumi or Terraform) and prefer changes made through code, not consoles.

 - Have operated high-throughput, data-intensive distributed systems in production, such as Druid, MongoDB, or Airflow, and understand scalability, fault tolerance, consistency trade-offs, and performance tuning.

 - Want to improve developer productivity, with CI/CD, tooling, and paved paths that let product engineers ship without owning infrastructure.

 - Experience with Apache Spark, Airflow, or TensorFlow.
